incoming.explanation: The analysis reasons over the deposition age datum, reading its rounded 'or thereabouts' character before deriving a birth window.
The age-heaping analysis reads the deposition's rounded 'or thereabouts 50' before any birth year is derived from it.

outgoing.explanation: The 1652/3 deposition age is the primary same-person anchor for the birth window and fixes its older end at c.1602/3.
The 1652/3 deposition age establishes the older Braintree John's approximate birth year for the de-conflation.

sources.excerpt: John Gurney of Brayntree aged 50 Yeares or therea-abouts. Dated 17-1-[16]52-3.
sources.locator: NEHGR vol. 62 (Jan. 1908), p. 94; Suffolk Court Files no. 188 ('22d paper')

finding.statement: In a Suffolk County deposition in Wilson v. Faxon, entered under Suffolk Court Files no. 188 and dated 17 (1st month) 1652/3 — 17 March 1652/3 old style — 'John Gurney of Brayntree' declared himself 'aged 50 Yeares or thereabouts'. It is his only surviving first-person statement of his own age.
